page: Google Cloud Platform x4-megamem-1440-metal is a bare-metal server in the Memory Optimized family designed for extreme-scale enterprise data operations. The machine runs on the x86_64 architecture, providing 1,440 dedicated vCPUs alongside 24,576 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 17.07 GB per vCPU, granting singular, non-virtualized access to substantial physical memory and compute capacity.

Hardware tradeoffs for the x4-megamem-1440-metal configuration include the absence of integrated GPU acceleration and zero bundled local storage. Storage operations must be routed through external cloud storage volumes. Furthermore, the configuration provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network management via virtual network gateways or dedicated IP assignment.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server concentrates massive memory density onto a single bare-metal deployment, avoiding the software overhead and latency associated with multi-node clustering for workloads that require a monolithic memory address space. The system is specifically targeted at mission-critical in-memory database engines such as SAP HANA, massive enterprise resource planning backends, and intensive real-time transactional analytics.
